feed.title: NPR Programs: All Things Considered
feed.subtitle: All Things Considered hosts Ailsa Chang, Mary Louise Kelly, Juana Summers and Scott Detrow present the program's trademark mix of news, interviews, commentaries, reviews, and offbeat features 7 days a week.

entry.title: 17 films to see before New Year's, from Oscar-bait to blockbusters
entry.summary: This winter, Pedro Pascal plays a cellist, Julianne Moore takes on community theater, and Andrew Garfield shows us Sam Altman's rise at the head of OpenAI.

entry.title: Trump effectively ended asylum. Advocates look to the Supreme Court to restore it
entry.summary: Trump's sweeping immigration changes — an asylum ban, mass firings and new legal maneuvers — have all but ended asylum. The high court will soon consider whether some shifts deny people due process.

entry.title: How 260 tons of Thanksgiving leftovers inspired an American icon: the TV dinner
entry.summary: The history behind the first TV dinner ties has a connection to Thanksgiving and tons of leftover frozen turkeys.

entry.title: After Democrats' midterm wins, some hope attacks on DEI will ease
entry.summary: After the midterms, a Democratic congressman declared that DEI is back. What does Democrats' ascendance portend for diversity initiatives that the Trump administration relentlessly attacked?

entry.title: A sweeping permitting reform bill is headed to the House. Critics want to stop it
entry.summary: President Trump supports a bipartisan bill that would speed up approval of federal infrastructure and energy projects. Critics say it will do so at the expense of the climate, tribes and public lands.

entry.title: This week in science: anxiety in college students, potatoes on the moon and whale snot
entry.summary: Science reporters Nate Rott and Sanden Totten talk about the growing risk of anxiety among college students, a simulation of growing potatoes on the Moon, and the genetic secrets in whale snot.

entry.title: Charrise Barron's new book unpacks the era when gospel crossed over into the mainstream
entry.summary: Ethnomusicologist Charrise Barron's new book, The Platinum Age of Gospel, looks at a ten year period between 1993 and 2013, when new artists pushed gospel beyond the church.

entry.title: The case for data centers
entry.summary: Most Americans do not like data centers. This Wisconsin mayor says voters have it wrong.

entry.title: The math community reacts to an AI-generated solution to a century-old math problem
entry.summary: A century's old hypothesis has been verified correct by AI. It's the latest discovery in mathematics, but will anyone every actually understand it?

entry.title: NPR's 'Here to Help' series looks back at volunteers helping older Americans
entry.summary: NPR's "Here to Help" series looks back at some volunteers featured in 2026 who focus on helping seniors in their communities.
